newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian troops killed, kidnap victim freed.
newsitem.headline: Colombian troops killed, kidnap victim freed.

text.p: As many as 25 soldiers were feared dead and scores were wounded or reported missing in fighting with leftist rebels in mountains just east of Bogota on Sunday, unnamed military sources told Colombian television.

The chief army spokeswoman was unable to confirm or deny the figures given in the TV Hoy news report. However, she said a number of soldiers had been killed, injured or were missing in the battle near San Juanito, about 30 miles (50 km) east of the capital.

If reports of the death toll were confirmed, it would be the heaviest blow to the army since rebels overran a military base in southern Colombia last August, killing 27 soldiers and taking 60 prisoners.

"There are soldiers dead and others have gone missing. But it is very difficult to get into the zone because of the intensity of the fighting and it is still to early to confirm any numbers," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
"Some troops are reported missing but we don't yet know if they have been captured or whether they have just taken cover," she added.
The battle broke out on Sunday morning when a 50-strong counter-insurgency unit came under fire from about 400 guerrillas of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the spokeswoman said.

Fighting erupted shortly after the army unit rescued a kidnapped Bogota businessman and French engineer Alain Fablet, who was captured by rebels last October as he worked for French company, Coyne et Bellier, on a highway construction project, military sources said.

The army spokeswoman added that the FARC contingent was thought to be an elite force in charge of guarding the guerrilla army's general secretariat, including its supreme commander Manuel Marulanda, alias "Sureshot".
An international spokesman for the FARC, however, denied the claim.
"That's pure rubbish invented by the army for propaganda purposes. The general secretariat is not pinned down or trapped in that zone by the army," Mexico City-based Marco Leon Calarca told Reuters.

Army helicopters carrying reinforcements came under fire and were forced to drop 160 troops miles (km) from the fighting and leave them to make their way on foot through treacherous terrain to the battle zone.
"As we flew helicopters into the battle zone, we came under fire. Two were hit; one pilot was injured and a soldier died," Gen. Juan Santos told TV Hoy.
